title: 被裁员后，他干到月入$2.4万
carouselChartTitle: 被裁员后，他干到月入$2.4万
author: 阿星
content:
## 冷启动：COVID让他失业，也让他觉醒

Ilya 在 Kyiv 的 KPI 读 Software Engineering。

大三时，拿到第一份 Ukrainian IT company 的工作。

给 US 和 European clients 做产品。

接下来三年，他做了 web platforms、mobile apps、marketplaces。

然后 COVID 来了。

他做的 project 开始 cutting costs。

一天，他发现自己 without a job。

去面了几家公司。

但很快 realized something：

**他不想再打工了。**

## 反直觉：$500存款开始的创业

他和被裁的 sales manager 同事一起。

Start outsourcing agency 叫 Quanti Coders。

类似之前的工作，但 redesigned everything to be faster、leaner、more effective。

Motto 是 "10x developers on demand"。

两年内，团队涨到7人。

给各种 exciting startups 做 web 和 mobile apps。

Fintech、healthcare、robotics。

目前月入约$15K。

第二年，他开始想：

What if we built our own product？

花了几周 searching for right idea。

Scrolling Indie Hackers。

Reading Trends。

Diving into Twitter founder threads。

然后他发现一个 gap：

没有好地方让 founders sell their apps。

Connect with other like-minded founders。

这个 gap 给了他 Microns 的 idea。

Cofounder 不 enthusiastic。

事实上，导致 falling out。

所以他决定 alone build Microns。

Working nights and weekends。

四年后，那个 "little side project" 成长为 main focus。

月入约$9K。

过去四年，helped just over a hundred founders sell their projects。

Combined total of more than $500K。

他 still part-time CTO at Quanti。

但 Microns 是他 energy 的主要去向。

## 暴击：战争的考验

最 tough 的时刻。

War started，Russia invaded his country。

He'd wake up at night to sound of missile explosions。

有些夜晚 entirely spent in shelters。

Next morning，try to keep working，completely exhausted。

战争最初几年，constant blackouts。

Walking dog in total darkness。

Coming home to no electricity。

Sometimes weeks without fuel。

Winters were especially brutal。

Looking back，he realizes those moments made him stronger。

He didn't give up。

He kept building。

Lost old team during that time。

One developer couldn't handle technical challenges。

Another went to work for competitor。

He realized communication was huge problem。

Rebuilt team with Ukrainians from different cities。

Fully remote but deeply connected by shared hardship。

Together，they built second version of Microns。

Custom design、user accounts、chat。

That launch helped them win first place on Product Hunt。

Gave motivation to keep pushing forward。

**Compared to living under daily threat of rockets and drones。**

Every other startup challenge feels small。

If he had to start over，he wouldn't change a thing。

Each challenge shaped him。

Tested his resilience。

Gave clarity to keep going。

That's what made him who he is today。

##  punchline：永不放弃，无论条件如何

Never give up，no matter the conditions。

Even if it feels like whole world is against you。

If you truly believe in what you're building，keep going。

当他开始时，plenty of people told him it wouldn't work。

Nobody would use it。

But you know your problem and your product better than anyone else。

Don't chase external validation。

Listen to your users instead。

Watch what they do。

Learn what they need。

Figure out how to solve their problems in a way they'll happily pay for。

And one more thing：

**Never go "all in" from day one。**

Start small，validate first，only then double down。
